verdict.rationale: Viam documents first-party fleet capabilities: a fleet management API covering organizations, locations, machines and "fragments", plus OTA software updates with canary testing and rollbacks. Together these suggest fleet-wide changes with some subset targeting. However, no evidence explains how a configuration change propagates to many machines at once, or how changes are targeted to a specific group. missing for 10: explicit docs that fragments push shared config to many machines simultaneously, documented per-group/per-location targeting of config rollouts, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an ops lead, I can push configuration changes across many robots at once with per-group targeting

citations.quote: With it you can create and manage organizations, locations, and individual machines, manage permissions and authorization, create and manage fragments
OTA updates for software and ML models; Canary testing and rollbacks for safe versioning
The fleet management API allows you to manage your machine fleet with code the same way you can do in the web UI.
No need to SSH into machines or stand next to robots for updates.
